text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination by itself — in structural engineering it reflects who holds senior posts, so it would be unremarkable even in a fair process. Raised alone, it sounds speculative and puts you on weak ground.

It does matter as context alongside the stronger facts: you had roughly double the experience, you were passed over on a soft, unmeasured criterion ("excellent client relationships"), and your request for written reasons has gone unanswered for two weeks.

So chase the written explanation first, in writing, with a deadline. Ask what the scoring criteria were and how each candidate scored. Mention panel composition only if the answer is evasive or the criteria look invented afterwards.
